items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: You hear Winger, you hear Muggsy, you hear Butterfield, you hear Yank Lawson. They all got different styles.

ctx.x: I got to hear him and meet him of course too. Is there any advice in playing together that is in harmonies or things that you work on, trumpet and trombone?

Paul is like Muggsy. You have what you call a good drive. And if the trumpet is driving, it makes you drive. That's what I feel. Of course I drive too. If I play with Bobby Haggard, Bobby plays a different style together. To me they all got different styles. You hear Winger, you hear Muggsy, you hear Butterfield, you hear Yank Lawson. They all got different styles.
Do you sometimes consciously try to play sort of a bass part since you don't usually use a string bass in your band or tuba?

items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: I think the closest thing to Bix today is Jimmie McPartland and Red Nichols.

ctx.x: Did his style sound somewhat like Bix, do you think? Some people have said that.
Yeah. Well, I think the closest thing to Bix today is Jimmie McPartland and Red Nichols.
Yeah. But did Emmett Hardy have that same kind of a style or was he more like the other, say, more like-
